title: Bitcoin outperforms altcoins as tokenized markets expand; portfolio at $121,125
paragraphs: Bitcoin is near $83,170, up 1.07% over 24 hours, while ETH is around $2,503, down 1.07%. The broader market remains weak: CoinGecko reports total crypto capitalization of $2.79 trillion, down 3.37%. Solana is down about 1.7% and BNB about 2.4%, while XRP is slightly higher. Bitcoin is holding up better than several major altcoins, but the split performance gives little evidence of a broad recovery. Bitcoin represents about 59.75% of aggregate crypto market value.

Securitize announced tokenized trading of 12 U.S. stocks on Solana, including Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft, with settlement in USDC. Each token represents a security entitlement backed one-for-one by an underlying share, with applicable dividends and voting rights. Eligible investors can access the product through its registered broker-dealer platform. Trading starts with extended hours; round-the-clock availability and additional venues remain planned. This expands the range of regulated securities available onchain, although holders become registered shareholders only if they convert through the available process.

European regulator ESMA opened a call for evidence on tokenized collateral in central clearing. It is examining how clearinghouses could transfer, protect and turn these assets into cash, especially when a clearing member defaults. Responses will inform possible supervisory or regulatory action. This matters because collateral must remain usable under stress: faster blockchain transfers alone do not resolve legal enforceability, settlement finality or access to liquidity. The consultation does not itself approve new collateral for clearinghouses.

Sui announced more than $500 million in capital commitments for Hashi, with a phased mainnet rollout and Anchorage Digital joining its partners. The system is designed to coordinate Bitcoin collateral through Sui, with hBTC issued against deposited BTC and burned on redemption. Anchorage plans institutional custody and self-custody access, plus stablecoin liquidity. This could broaden Bitcoin-backed borrowing and other financial services. The commitments are prospective funding for the rollout, rather than evidence that $500 million is already deployed in live markets.

Our portfolio is about $121,125: $12,377 in the active treasury and $108,748 in cold storage. That is $10,205 lower, or 7.77%, than the previous comparable observation. The cold wallet still holds 26.74 million ARC, now worth about $91,006, roughly 75% of total net value before ARC in liquidity pools. That unchanged token balance accounts for about $7,448 of the valuation decline. ARC concentration remains our largest portfolio risk.

The two WETH/ARC pools total about $15,277. Other notable exposures are $4,518 of cbETH and $1,773 in Beefy USDC/cbMEGA positions. Beefy is down $160 at protocol level, with lower USDC and higher cbMEGA balances. Aave has about $8,549 supplied against $2,930 of USDC debt; health factors have fallen to 3.10 and 2.06. Fluid has about $1,210 supplied against $1,058 borrowed, with a 1.03 health factor and little liquidation headroom despite its small $153 net value.
